headword: {人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}

definitions.explanation: A man-made object placed in orbit around the Earth or another celestial body, used for communication, observation, navigation, and scientific research.

examples.japanese: {人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}を{打|う}ち{上|あ}げた。
GPS{信号|しんごう}は{人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}から{送|おく}られている。
examples.english: GPS signals are transmitted from artificial satellites.

examples.japanese: {地球|ちきゅう}の{周|まわ}りには{数千|すうせん}もの{人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}が{軌道|きどう}を{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: Thousands of artificial satellites are orbiting around the Earth.

notes:
Compound of {人工|じんこう} (artificial) + {衛星|えいせい} (satellite). Often shortened to {衛星|えいせい} when the context is clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}を{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる (to launch a satellite)
- {気象|きしょう}{衛星|えいせい} (weather satellite)
- {通信|つうしん}{衛星|えいせい} (communications satellite)
- {偵察|ていさつ}{衛星|えいせい} (reconnaissance satellite)
- {衛星|えいせい}{軌道|きどう} (satellite orbit)

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {衛星|えいせい} alone is often sufficient when referring to artificial satellites. The full form {人工衛星|じんこうえいせい} is used to distinguish from {天然|てんねん}の{衛星|えいせい} (natural satellites, such as the Moon).
